description: Water-soil and climate scores for three illustrative rotations. Pest and market pillars are outside this file.

scoreMethod.water: score = 5 * (max net irrigation - scenario net irrigation) / (max - min) across the three scenarios. A score of 5 is only the lowest demand in this set.
scoreMethod.climate: score = 5 * (1 - fraction of cycle days in heat-risk or dry-quartile calendar months).
scoreMethod.rainfallProduct: POWER PRECTOTCORR because IMERG millimetres were not available without Earthdata Login.

scoreScale.direction: Higher means lower estimated net irrigation demand than the other scenarios in this file.

pillars.summary: Red bean then maize needs about 433.152 mm of net irrigation in this POWER climatology (806.143 mm ETc and 414.761 mm effective rain). Soil moisture, slope, and texture are missing, so the soil part of the pillar is not scored.

metrics.label: Net irrigation demand

provenance.citation: 2016-2025 daily POWER point used as the climatology for both pillars.

metrics.limitation: ETc minus USDA-SCS effective rain from POWER precipitation. IMERG was not available. Soil storage is ignored. Relative scores use only the three scenarios in this file.

metrics.label: Crop evapotranspiration

provenance.citation: 2016-2025 daily POWER point used as the climatology for both pillars.

metrics.limitation: FAO-56 Kc curve times POWER Penman-Monteith ET0. Stage lengths are published examples, not local observations.

metrics.label: Effective rainfall credited to the sequence

provenance.citation: 2016-2025 daily POWER point used as the climatology for both pillars.

metrics.limitation: POWER rainfall, not IMERG. The technical plan keeps POWER tropical rainfall out of the principal rainfall product.

reviewRisks: Scenario, discuss with a local technician.
POWER cell elevation is higher than the valley floor described by the team, so temperature and ET0 may not match a field.
Bean sowing is 15 November, inside the 5 November-15 December window cited from the IDIAF compendium. It is not an optimal date. Maize starts the next day.

scoreScale.direction: Higher means a smaller share of cycle days falls in climatological heat-risk or dry-quartile months.

pillars.summary: About 41.3 percent of the template cycle falls in a heat-risk or dry-quartile month at the POWER point. Heat-risk months are [7, 8, 9]. Dry-quartile months are [1, 2, 3].

metrics.label: Fraction of cycle days in heat-risk or dry-quartile months

provenance.citation: 2016-2025 daily POWER point used as the climatology for both pillars.

metrics.limitation: Heat-risk months are the upper quartile of climatological mean Tmax. Dry-quartile months are the lowest quartile of POWER rainfall. This is not a yield or pest forecast.

metrics.label: Historical POWER drought months in 2016-2025

provenance.citation: 2016-2025 daily POWER point used as the climatology for both pillars.

metrics.limitation: Same count for every scenario. It describes the point climatology, not a difference between rotations.

missingData: A crop-specific heat threshold validated for San Juan
